definitions.explanation: A round, open-topped container traditionally made of wood, used for carrying water, bathing, or storage. In modern use, also refers to plastic basins and tubs.

examples.japanese: {風呂|ふろ}{桶|おけ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦お{湯|ゆ}→お湯：02518_oyu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけた→かける：00854_kakeru⟧。
examples.english: I poured hot water with a bath bucket.
I put water in a wooden tub and arranged flowers in it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{桶|おけ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}っていた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: In the old days, craftsmen in this area used to make handcrafted wooden buckets.

notes:
USAGE:
Traditionally refers to wooden containers made by coopers ({桶屋|おけや}). In modern everyday life, most commonly encountered as {風呂|ふろ}{桶|おけ} (bath bucket used for scooping water in Japanese-style bathing). Also appears in the well-known proverb ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{吹|ふ}けば→吹く：02445_fuku⟧{桶屋|おけや}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{儲|もう}かる (when the wind blows, the bucket-maker profits — a chain of unlikely cause and effect).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風呂|ふろ}{桶|おけ}: bath bucket
- {木|き}{桶|おけ}: wooden bucket
- {桶屋|おけや}: bucket-maker, cooper
- ⟦{寿司|すし}{桶|おけ}→寿司桶：08131_sushioke⟧: sushi serving tub

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦バケツ→バケツ：11118_baketsu⟧: bucket (Western-style, usually metal or plastic, with a handle)
